calibration_rule: Within one layer, select the four heads with the largest mean first-order source-max gain: transferred source-max mass times the local source-versus-donor output-margin utility gap. Choose the layer with the largest top-four sum.
calibration_isolation: Calibration uses RNG seed 100000 + seed. Evaluation uses RNG seed equal to seed. Evaluation outcomes are not used for circuit selection.
matched_baseline: Repeat the same evaluation examples with the original natural-source-mass selector.
primary_estimand: Utility-selected source-max minus spectrum-preserving distractor-control output-margin change.
selector_estimand: The utility-selected source-max-minus-control effect minus the source-mass-selected source-max-minus-control effect on paired examples.
competence_gate: A length is confirmatory only when mean untouched baseline exact-match accuracy across seeds is at least 0.50.
primary_success_rule: At every confirmatory length, the pooled paired 95% interval for the primary estimand excludes zero on the positive side, and the pooled selector estimand is positive.
secondary_predictions: Utility-selected source-min lowers the output margin at competent lengths.
Calibration mean predicted gain ranks intervention benefit better than natural source mass.
Length 80 is diagnostic if baseline competence remains below 0.50.
interpretation_if_pass: Supports the theorem's conditional claim that attention assignment must be combined with downstream utility when selecting intervention circuits.
interpretation_if_fail: Shows that the local first-order utility term is not sufficient as a cross-architecture intervention-selection rule; retain it as an explanatory local condition rather than a practical selector.
